title: Extension strategies: Crunch Bites
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 43 (Pupil PDF worksheet: own exam-style questions, case data and mark-scheme points (teacher-written))
intro: Lesson 43. Choose the best extension strategy using the data. All businesses, people and figures in these cases are fictional, made up for practice.

passage.title: Crunch Bites
paras: Crunch Bites is a halal crisp brand launched in 2021. Sales have stopped growing and a rival has launched a cheaper own-brand crisp. The marketing budget for next year is £200,000. Three options: sell in supermarkets in the Gulf (new market); launch three new flavours; new multipack packaging for lunchboxes.

questions.q: Which stage of the product life cycle is Crunch Bites in? Use the data.
questions.a: Maturity moving into saturation or early decline: growth slowed (450 to 455) then sales fell to 440.

questions.q: Evaluate the best extension strategy for Crunch Bites.
questions.a: Level-marked (12): weigh new market (large growth potential, but export costs, certification and risk), new flavours (cheaper, refreshes interest, may cannibalise), new packaging (cheap, targets families, may not stop decline); judgement that depends on cost within £200,000 and the rival's price cut.

frame.label: For: point and chain of reasoning in context
Against: point and chain of reasoning in context
Judgement: decide, give the main reason, say what it depends on

markScheme.a: Level 4 (10-12): developed chains on both sides in context and a supported judgement with 'it depends on'. Level 3 (7-9): both sides developed, judgement partly supported. Level 2 (4-6): some development, one-sided or generic. Level 1 (1-3): points identified.
